chapters.first-impression: Okay, Gap. Here's what people clock in the first ten seconds: confidence, opinions, and posture like you're about to give a talk nobody booked. You walk in like the room should rearrange itself around you. Half the time it does, which is annoying for everyone else and great for you. People assume you're in charge, so they hand you things: projects, problems, the restaurant booking. You take them, obviously. What they don't see right away is that you're quite sensitive about being respected. You'd rather be right than liked. You'd prefer both. And you get grumpy when you can only pick one. That's the read. You're welcome.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag? You don't bend. At all. A tree grows straight up, and you've decided that's a personality trait instead of a botanical fact. You'll listen to feedback, nod thoughtfully, and then do exactly what you'd already planned. You call it conviction. Everyone else calls it the reason they say can someone else talk to Gap. Being stubborn about values is admirable. Being stubborn about which route to the cinema is just tiring for the people in the car. Bom says you're principled. I say you're principled about things that are not principles. Learn the difference and you'll be unstoppable instead of merely unmovable.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love, you lead. You plan the dates, the trips, the five-year outline nobody asked to see. Partners love it at first, then quietly realise they're passengers in their own relationship. Your sabotage move is deciding what the relationship is and then being genuinely confused when the other person has opinions about it. You also pick people who need you, because being needed feels like being loved, and then resent carrying them. That's a loop, and you built it. Try someone who wants to walk beside you, not behind you. And when they disagree, say tell me more before you start drafting your rebuttal. Revolutionary, I know.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you end up leading even when nobody hired you to. Great for your career, slightly terrifying for your coworkers, who have learned to just agree in meetings. You're fair, driven, and convinced that I'll just do it myself is a strategy. It's not. It's a burnout plan with good branding. With friends you're loyal to the bone. You'll show up for the move, the breakup, the crisis at 1am. But you give advice like you're billing by the hour. Sometimes your friends don't want a five-point plan. They want you to say that sucks. Two words. You can manage two words.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm fine, I just have a lot going on. You always have a lot going on, because you keep adding things to the pile and calling it ambition. You treat rest like a reward you haven't quite earned yet. You also tell yourself you don't need anyone's approval, which is adorable, because you absolutely want respect from the people you respect. That's not weakness, Gap. It's being a person. Admit it, out loud if you're brave, and you'll stop overworking to earn something the people who matter are already giving you.
chapters.the-fix: Fine. Bom made me add a fix chapter, so here it is. Bend a little, on purpose, on small things. Let someone else pick the restaurant and don't comment on the menu. Ask one question a day that you don't already know the answer to. Rest before you're empty, not after you've collapsed. In love, choose someone strong enough to tell you no, and then actually let them win sometimes. You're a tall tree. You give shade, structure and direction to a lot of people. You'll be even better when you stop treating flexibility like an attack. Okay. I'm done being nice. That was a lot for me.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap. You walk in like the room owes you an agenda.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's called leadership, Yeon.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: It's called refusing to let anyone else pick the restaurant.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your red flag: you don't bend. Trees can sway, you know.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: But Gap is so loyal and fair!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. Now say 'tell me more' before the rebuttal. Practise.

chapters.first-impression: Eul, people meet you and think: oh, they're lovely. Easy to talk to, warm, funny, somehow already on first-name terms with the barista. You read rooms like a professional and adjust in real time. Ten seconds in, people feel comfortable. Ten minutes in, they've told you about their childhood and their ex. What they don't notice is that you're also quietly checking whether they like you. Constantly. You're charming partly because you're working at it, a little, all the time. Which is fine. Just know that it's work, and you're allowed to clock out whenever you like.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you're a professional chameleon. You become whatever the person in front of you seems to want, and you're so good at it that you sometimes forget your own colour. I don't mind, whatever you want. You do mind. You mind a lot, three days later, in the shower, rehearsing what you should have said. You call it being flexible. It's actually avoiding conflict with a smile. And eventually the resentment leaks out sideways, in some weird little comment, and everyone's confused about where it came from. Have the opinion at the time. It's cheaper.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you wrap around people like a vine around a fence, and then wonder why you can't leave the fence. Your sabotage is over-adapting. You change your music, your schedule, your whole vibe, and then feel unseen. Well, yes. You hid. You also sometimes stay with people who are just okay, because being alone feels like being left unwatered. You are not a houseplant. You can survive a weekend by yourself, I promise. Try it. And say what you actually want on the first date. It's attractive, it saves months, and the right person will be relieved.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're the glue. Everyone likes you, you smooth over tensions, clients adore you. You also volunteer for things you don't want to do, because saying no feels rude. With friends you're the heart of the group chat, the one who remembers birthdays and sends the voice note at the right moment. But you have that one friend who drains you, and you keep showing up anyway. Why? Because you hate disappointing people more than you hate being tired. Here's the news: your energy is not a public utility. People can't just plug in.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm easygoing. No. You're accommodating, which is a completely different thing. Easygoing people don't keep a mental list of every time they compromised. You also tell yourself you're not that strong. Please. You've bounced back from things that would knock a tree flat. You're tougher than anyone in your life realises, including you. Stop introducing yourself as the delicate one. The delicate one doesn't survive half of what you've survived and then still turn up to brunch with a smile. Honestly, you're the vine growing through concrete. Act like it.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, by request of Bom, who is hovering. Have one preference a day, out loud. Restaurant, film, the temperature of the room, I don't care which. Say no once a week without giving a reason. Spend one evening alone and enjoy it on purpose, no apologies. In love, ask early what they want, and tell them what you want in the same conversation. You are incredibly adaptable, and that really is a gift. Use it to grow toward the light, not toward whoever happens to be standing closest. Okay, Bom, I said something nice. Happy?

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul. You've said 'I don't mind' eleven times today.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul is just easygoing!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul keeps a secret list of every compromise. I've seen it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You change your whole vibe for every crush. Pick a colour.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul's warmth is real, though.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: So is that backbone. Use it. Say no once this week.

chapters.first-impression: Byeong, you don't enter a room, you happen to it. Ten seconds in, people know your name, your opinion on the playlist, and that you're the fun one. You're warm, generous, a little loud, and genuinely delightful. People feel seen by you, which is your real magic. What they also clock: you need an audience. Not in a bad way. You just light up when people are watching and dim slightly when they're not. That isn't vanity. That's a sun noticing it's daytime. Still, it's worth knowing that everyone can tell when you're on.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you overshare, overcommit and overexplain, all before lunch. You say yes to every plan because you love people, then cancel two of them because you're exhausted. You're honest to the point of did you really have to say that at the table. And when you're hurt, you don't hide it. The whole room gets the weather report, with satellite images. Openness is lovely. A little filter is also lovely. You're allowed to have both. They're not mutually exclusive, no matter what your mouth has been telling you.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you go big and fast. Grand gestures, enormous feelings, a shared playlist by week two. Partners feel like they're in a film and then start wondering when the credits roll. Your sabotage is burning hot and getting bored, or falling for people who are cool and distant because the chase is fun. Spoiler: a cold person doesn't warm up because you shine harder. They just get a tan. Try someone who's warm back. It will feel less exciting at first. It will also feel like being loved, which is better.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're the energy. Brainstorms, team mood, the presentation everyone remembers for weeks. Follow-through? Let's discuss it. You start ten things and finish four, brilliantly. With friends you're the host, the hype person, the one who organises everyone's birthday. But you can take it personally when people don't match your energy. Not everyone runs at your voltage. That's not rejection. That's just the difference between lamps and suns. Lamps are fine. Lamps are cosy. Let them be lamps without reading it as a review of you. And maybe hand the spreadsheet part to someone who enjoys it.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm fine, I'm always fine. You're the happy one, so you feel like you're not allowed a bad day. Wrong. You also tell yourself that being liked by everyone matters. It really doesn't. Being loved by a few matters, and those few want to see you on a cloudy day too. They're not booking you for the sunshine. They're booking you for you. Let them see the weather sometimes, without turning it into a show. Quietly sad is allowed. The people worth keeping will stay through a grey week. That's how you'll know who they are.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, because Bom is pouting. Finish one thing before you start the next. Pause three seconds before the honest comment and check whether it's kind as well as true. Schedule one evening a week with nothing in it: no plans, no audience, no content. In love, slow the first month down and look for someone who's warm, not someone you have to defrost. Your light is the best thing about you. Just stop spending all of it on other people's rooms. Save some for your own. There. Bom is beaming. Disgusting.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, you said yes to four plans tonight. It's Tuesday.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong just loves people!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Loves people, then cancels by voice note. From the bath.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also, a cold crush doesn't melt because you shine harder.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong makes everyone feel seen.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Agreed. Now pick someone who's warm back. Radical.

chapters.first-impression: Jeong, people meet you and feel like you're paying attention. Because you are. Ten seconds in, you've noticed their mood, their nervous hands, and that the person beside them is lying about something. You're warm but not loud, a candle rather than a bonfire. People feel safe telling you things. What they don't see: you're also deciding whether they're safe for you. And most of them don't pass. You're friendly with many and close to very few, and the few have no idea how hard the exam was. Maybe make the exam a little easier.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you overthink. Professionally. One ambiguous text and you've written a three-act play, cast it, and cried at the ending. You also hold onto hurts, quietly, for years. You'll say it's fine and then remember the exact date it wasn't. And your mood can change the temperature of a room without you saying a single word. You don't need to stop feeling deeply. Please don't. You need to tell people what you feel before it hardens into a grudge they didn't know they were earning. Say it small and early. It's kinder.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you're intense, devoted, and very attentive. Wonderful. Also occasionally a lot. Your sabotage move is reading signs instead of asking questions. They're quiet, you assume they're losing interest, you pull back first to protect yourself, and now they're confused about why you've gone cold. It's a self-fulfilling candle. Ask. Use your words. You're fantastic with words when you're not scared. And remember that not everyone who's calm is cold. Some people are just calm. It's a personality, not a verdict. Before you pull back, send one honest text instead. You'll be amazed how often it fixes everything.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're the one who notices what everyone else missed: the detail, the nuance, the vibe in the meeting. But you take criticism personally and replay it at 1am like a podcast nobody asked for. With friends you're the deep-talk friend, the one people call when it's real. You also keep score a little, quietly. Who replied, who forgot, who didn't ask. Your friends aren't always failing you. Sometimes they're just busy, tired, or bad at texting. Give them the benefit of the doubt you'd want. Also, delete the 1am podcast. Nobody's listening.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm just being realistic. No. Sometimes you're being scared and calling it realism because it sounds wiser. You also tell yourself that if you show all your feelings, people will leave. Some might. The right ones won't. Hiding your feelings doesn't keep people close. It just means they end up loving a version of you with the volume turned right down, and you end up lonely in a room full of people who like you. Turn the volume up one notch this week. Just one. See who leans in instead of leaving.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, because Bom keeps tapping my shoulder. Give your overthinking a timer: twenty minutes, then do something with your hands. Say one hurt out loud within a day of it happening, not a year later in a fight about something else. Assume good intent once a day, as a little experiment, and see what happens. In love, ask the question instead of reading the sign. You have the most beautiful kind of light, the close, warm kind. Let people sit near it without testing them first. Most of them only want to get warm.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Jeong. You've reread that text nine times. It says 'ok'.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong is just very perceptive!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Perceptive, yes. Also writing a tragedy about a full stop.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You pull back first so nobody can leave you. Clever. Exhausting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong loves so deeply, though.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. So ask the question. Words. Out loud. Today.

chapters.first-impression: Mu, people meet you and feel calmer. You're solid, unbothered, the human equivalent of a very good sofa. Ten seconds in they think: this person could handle a crisis. You could, and you have, several times, without making a fuss. You don't perform, don't oversell, don't rush. What they also clock: you're hard to read. Is Mu happy? Annoyed? Asleep with eyes open? Nobody knows. Not even, on some days, you. You've perfected the neutral face so well that you sometimes forget there's weather behind it. Let someone in on the forecast sometimes.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you don't move. Physically, emotionally, philosophically. You've had the same opinion since 2014 and you're proud of it. New idea? You'll consider it. For about two years. And when you're upset, you go silent and heavy, like weather that refuses to break, while everyone tiptoes around the mountain wondering what they did. Stability is a real gift. Stubbornness dressed up as stability is just stubbornness with better posture. Learn which one you're doing, and admit it when it's the second. Hint: if you can't explain why, it's probably the second one.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you're loyal, protective, and as reliable as sunrise. Partners feel safe. They also feel occasionally bored, and sometimes lonely next to you, because you show love by doing and very rarely by saying. You fix the shelf. You don't say I love how you laugh. Your sabotage is assuming they know. They don't. You also stay too long in things because leaving feels like relocating a mountain. Say one loving thing out loud once a week. It won't kill you. I checked the research. It's fine. Start with something easy, like I like having you here.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're the rock. Deadlines, crises, the person people trust with the things that actually matter. But you resist change, new systems, new tools, new ideas, until it's very late and slightly embarrassing. With friends you're the one who shows up, helps carry the sofa, never forgets the important date. But you rarely ask for help yourself, so people genuinely don't know when you need it. They're not psychic, Mu. Give them a chance to carry something for you, even something small. They'd actually love to. People like repaying mountains.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm not really an emotional person. Mu, you have feelings the size of a mountain range. You just keep them underground, where they come out as tiredness, irritation, or a sudden eruption over how someone loaded the dishwasher. You also tell yourself change is risky. Sometimes it is. But staying exactly the same is also a risk. It's just a slower one, so you don't notice it until you're standing in the same spot, wondering why the view never changes. Move one rock this month. Just one. See how the view changes.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, by order of Bom. Try one new thing a month: a food, a route, an opinion, a playlist. Say one feeling out loud a day, even a tiny one. I'm tired counts. Ask a friend for help with something small so everyone learns you're allowed to need things. In love, use words as well as actions, at least once a week. You're the steadiest person in most rooms. Imagine how good you'd be with a little movement. A mountain with a breeze. Honestly, iconic. Don't tell Bom I said that.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, you've had the same opinion since 2014.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's called being consistent!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: It's called refusing to try the new café. For three years.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also, fixing their shelf isn't saying 'I love you'. Use words.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu is the most reliable person ever.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Yes. Reliable people can still say 'I'm sad'. Try it.

chapters.first-impression: Gi, people meet you and want to tell you everything. You're warm, practical, with strong mum-friend energy whatever your age. Ten seconds in, you've offered them water, a snack, or a solution. You notice who's uncomfortable and quietly fix it. What they don't see: you're also worrying. About them, about the plan, about whether you said something weird three minutes ago. Your brain runs a background app called What Could Go Wrong, and it never closes. Not even on holiday. Especially not on holiday. Maybe close a few tabs before bed.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you overgive, then quietly resent it. You'll do the favour, the planning, the emotional heavy lifting, and say it's no trouble at all. Then one day you snap about the dishes and everyone's shocked. It was never about the dishes. It was the last forty things. You also worry so much that you sometimes control. I'm just helping can mean I'm managing you. Let people fail a little. It builds character. Theirs, not yours. Yours is already very well built, thank you. Say the small annoyance when it's still small, before it turns into a dishwasher incident.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you nurture like it's your calling. You cook, remember, plan, comfort. Partners feel cherished, and some of them also get very comfortable and stop doing much at all. Your sabotage is picking people who need a lot of care, because being needed feels safe, and then feeling invisible while you run their life. You deserve someone who notices you're tired before you say it. Also, stop apologising when you ask for things. A request isn't a burden. It's information about how to love you. Write it down if saying it feels too hard.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're the person who knows where everything is and somehow ends up doing three jobs for the price of one. You're dependable, organised, and far too nice about extra tasks. With friends you're the caretaker, the planner, the one who checks in after the hard appointment. But you rarely let anyone check in on you. Being strong for everyone isn't a medal. It's just tiring, and nobody's giving out trophies for it. Let someone else host for once and simply turn up with nothing. Bring nothing. Not even a dessert.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: it's easier if I just do it. Easier now, much harder later, when you're resentful and exhausted and nobody understands why. You also tell yourself your needs are small. They're not small. They're just quiet. Quiet needs still need meeting, and the people who love you would actually like to meet them, if you'd stop hiding the list. Hand it over. Let them be useful to you for a change. Start small: tell one person one thing you need this week, and then let them actually do it without you supervising.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, because Bom made a face at me. Say no to one favour a week. Let one person take care of you, and don't repay them within the same hour. Catch yourself apologising and swap sorry for thank you. In love, look for someone who tends your garden too, not just someone who enjoys the view. Close the worry app at night: write it all down, then sleep. You make everyone around you grow. You get to grow too. Write that on a sticky note. Put it on the fridge you clean for everyone.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gi. You've apologised six times today. For existing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi is just considerate!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gi runs a free care service with no opening hours.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And 'I'm just helping' sometimes means 'I'm managing you'.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: But everyone loves Gi!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They do. So let one of them make you dinner. No repaying.

chapters.first-impression: Gyeong, people meet you and feel slightly intimidated, then slightly impressed. You're direct, decisive, and you don't fake interest in anything. Ten seconds in, they know whether you like them, because your face has no privacy settings. You're loyal, fair, and you'd fight for your people without being asked. What they don't see right away: you're actually soft about the few you love. Very soft. You just guard it like a bank vault with a moat and a slightly scary security guard, who is also you. Maybe lower the drawbridge occasionally.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you're blunt. Sometimes surgically. You say the true thing with zero padding and then can't understand why someone's upset. I was just being honest. Yes. Honesty without kindness is just a sharp object being waved around a kitchen. You also see the world in black and white, and grey makes you angry. Most of life is grey. Annoying, I know. You can keep the blade. Just learn to put it back in its sheath when you're having a conversation instead of a duel. Same truth, gentler delivery. Still counts.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you're loyal to the bone. Once you choose, you choose, and that's rare and wonderful. But you can be hard to approach and harder to argue with. Your sabotage is treating disagreements like battles to win, and cutting people off fast when they disappoint you. One mistake and the file is closed and archived. Some people deserve a second look. Also, say soft things sometimes. Your partner knows you'd fight a bear for them. They would also like a compliment about their hair. Both matter. Give them both. You have plenty of each.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're decisive and brilliant in a crisis. You also have zero patience for incompetence, and it shows: on your face, in meetings, in the way you type. With friends you're the one who'd help hide the evidence, metaphorically, of course. Loyal forever. But you drop people quickly when they cross a line, and your lines aren't always visible to anyone except you. Tell people where the lines are. They can't respect a boundary they've never been shown. A quick heads-up costs you one sentence and saves a whole friendship. Very efficient. You'll love it.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I don't care what people think. You care a great deal about what your people think. You care about being respected and being seen as fair. You also tell yourself that being tough means not getting hurt. It doesn't. It means you get hurt and don't show it, which is a completely different thing and much heavier to carry. Ask yourself who's protecting you while you're busy protecting everyone else. If the answer is nobody, that's worth fixing. Let one person in on the armour.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, at Bom's insistence. Before saying the true thing, add one kind sentence in front of it. Ask one question before you deliver a verdict. Allow one second chance this year, where it's actually deserved. In love, say the soft thing: I appreciate you. It's not weakness. It's precision, applied to feelings. You're the most loyal person most people will ever meet. Imagine if they also felt safe disagreeing with you. That would make you basically unbeatable, which I know you'd enjoy. Start with the kind sentence. Start today. Start with someone who'll be very confused.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, you called their haircut 'a choice'. They cried.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong was just being honest.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Honesty without kindness is a knife in a nice outfit.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also, one mistake and you archive people. Bit much.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong is the most loyal friend ever, though.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. Add one kind sentence before the verdict. Every time.

chapters.first-impression: Sin, people meet you and think: put together. The outfit, the posture, the very specific coffee order. You notice everything and you're polite about it, mostly. Ten seconds in, people can tell you have taste, and maybe also that you're slightly judging their shoes. You are. We both know you are. What they don't see: you're sensitive. Very. A careless comment can sting for days behind a perfectly composed face, and you'll replay it while doing your skincare, word by word. Maybe tell someone when it happens, out loud, on the day.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: perfectionism with a side of silent judgment. You have standards for everything, and you grade everyone quietly, then feel disappointed when they fail criteria they didn't know existed. You also take small slights personally and keep them polished in a little display case, lit nicely, labelled by date. People think you're cool and above it. Actually, you're hurt and far too elegant to say so. That's a lot of energy spent on looking unbothered when you could just mention it. Saying that stung is extremely chic, actually.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you want to be treasured, and you should be. But you sometimes test people instead of telling them what you need. Your sabotage is falling for an ideal and then being let down by the real, slightly chaotic human. You also play it cool when you care, waiting hours to reply so you seem unbothered. Unbothered isn't attractive. Honest is. Real people have flaws. So do real jewels, by the way. They're called inclusions, and they're how you tell a real stone from a fake one. Be the real one.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you deliver quality: polished, precise, impeccable. Also slow, because nothing is ever finished, it's just abandoned at 2am when you finally give up on perfect. Criticism hurts far more than you let anyone see. With friends you're thoughtful, the perfect gift giver, the one with the excellent recommendations. But you can be picky about friends to the point of loneliness. Not everyone needs to be fully polished to be worth keeping. Some of the best people are a bit rough around the edges. Let a few of them in.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I just have high standards. Sometimes it's high standards. Sometimes it's fear of being seen trying and failing in public. You also tell yourself you're fine alone because people are disappointing. Some are, sure. But some would genuinely surprise you if you let them see the unpolished version: the bad day, the messy room, the unfiltered opinion. That version is more lovable than you think. It's certainly more interesting. Show one person the messy draft of you this month. Watch them like you more, not less. It's almost annoying how well it works.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, approved by Bom. Finish something at ninety percent and send it anyway. Tell one person something that hurt, right when it happens, in plain words. Do one thing badly on purpose: karaoke, a sketch, dancing at a wedding. In love, say what you need instead of testing whether they'll guess. You're a jewel: rare, sharp, beautiful. You don't need to be flawless to be precious. Nobody does. Not even you. Especially not you. Okay, that was almost sweet. Moving on. Seriously, ninety percent is plenty. Nobody else can see the last ten.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin. You've judged three outfits and a font since we started.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin just has great taste!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Great taste. And a secret scorecard nobody agreed to.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You play it cool when you care. Unbothered isn't a love language.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin is so thoughtful, though.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. Now do karaoke badly. On purpose. Character building.

chapters.first-impression: Im, people meet you and feel like they've walked into a fun, slightly elusive story. You're curious, clever, adventurous, with three fascinating anecdotes and a trip coming up. Ten seconds in, they want to know you. Ten weeks in, they're still trying to pin you down. What they don't see: your mind is always somewhere else, half planning the next thing, the next city, the next idea. You're present, mostly. About eighty percent. The other twenty is already boarding a different flight. It's charming. It's also very obvious to everyone sitting with you.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you disappear. Not dramatically. You just drift, stop replying, go and do your own thing for a week, then come back like nothing happened. To you, it's freedom. To everyone else, it's a slightly anxious are we okay? You also avoid commitment like it's a parking ticket. And you can turn cool when things get emotional, retreating into logic. Let's think about this rationally is not a hug. Nobody in tears has ever wanted a flowchart. A two-line heads-up before you vanish would solve about ninety percent of this.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you bring excitement, spontaneity, and huge conversations at 3am. Partners feel like life got bigger. Then they try to make plans for next month and you get strange about it. Your sabotage is leaving emotionally the moment something feels like a cage, even if the cage is just my parents would like to meet you. Commitment isn't a prison. It's a home port. You can sail as far as you like and still come back to the same harbour. That's the whole point of a harbour. Try staying for one dinner.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're the visionary: big ideas, strong strategy, terrible with forms. You get bored with routine and sometimes leave the boring part for someone else to finish. With friends you're the adventure friend, the one with a plan for the spontaneous weekend. But you're hard to reach. Your replies are basically seasonal. Your friends miss you, and they're too polite to say how much. Answer the group chat. They've started a poll on whether you still exist. One reply a week would change everything. They're not asking for a novel, just a sign of life.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I just value my freedom. Sometimes it's freedom. Sometimes it's avoidance wearing a very nice coat. You also tell yourself you don't really get attached. You do. You just leave before anyone sees it, including you. That isn't independence. That's running, in good shoes, with a great playlist. Admitting that you care doesn't anchor you forever. It just means someone finally gets to know where you are. Try saying I missed you to someone, before you leave again. It won't trap you. It'll just feel unfamiliar, then good, in that order.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, because Bom demanded it. Reply within a day, even if it's just busy, love you, talk soon. Finish one boring task each week, fully, to the very end. Stay in one emotional conversation until it's actually over, no logic exit halfway through. In love, try one small commitment and notice that nothing terrible happens. You're the ocean: deep and free. Everyone wants some of that. Let someone stand on the shore and wave you home. You might even like the wave. Start with the group chat. Today. Right now, actually.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im. You replied to my message from March. It's not March.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im is just very free-spirited!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Free-spirited. Also emotionally on another continent.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'Let's think about this rationally' is not a hug, Im.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Life is so exciting with Im around.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Agreed. Now answer the group chat. They think you vanished.

chapters.first-impression: Gye, people meet you and feel oddly understood. You're gentle, observant, a little mysterious, with soft energy that makes people relax without knowing why. Ten seconds in, you've picked up their mood and matched it. They feel like you get them. You do. What they don't see: you've also absorbed their stress, and you'll carry it home like a souvenir nobody asked you to buy. You're basically a sponge in a nice jumper, and you go home much heavier than you arrived. Wring yourself out before bed. Seriously, every night.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you're vague. Maybe. We'll see. Whatever you want. You hint instead of asking, then feel hurt when nobody picks up on the hint. You also retreat into your imagination when life gets hard, which is cosy but isn't a plan. And you can be a bit secretive, sharing the weather report but never the forecast. Mystery is charming on a first date. By month six, it's just confusing, and the people who love you are tired of guessing. Give them the forecast. They can handle it, I promise.
chapters.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you're tender, intuitive, deeply romantic, the partner who senses something's wrong before a word is said. Beautiful. Your sabotage is expecting that same skill in return. If they loved me, they'd know. They don't know. They're not a weather app. You also sometimes fall for the idea of someone more than the actual person, because your imagination is very generous with the details. Say your needs. In words. Specific ones. Whole sentences, ideally with a verb. Try one this week and watch how relieved they look. Genuinely relieved.
chapters.friends-and-work: At work you're creative and perceptive, wonderful with people and good at reading what a client really wants. But you drift when things feel meaningless, and you avoid conflict like it's a wasp at a picnic. With friends you're the empathetic one, the one who just gets it. But you absorb their problems until you're completely drained, then vanish for a week to recover, and nobody knows why you went quiet. Tell them. You're allowed to need a recharge. A simple I need a quiet week, love you, sorts it.
chapters.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm just a private person. Sometimes it's privacy. Sometimes it's the fear that if people see the real you, it'll be too much for them. It won't. You also tell yourself that you don't need much. You need a lot, actually, emotionally, and that's completely okay. Needing a lot isn't a flaw. Hiding it and hoping someone will notice is the part that keeps going wrong. Stop hiding it. Start with one person who's earned it. Tell them one real thing. Then breathe. Then do it again next week.
chapters.the-fix: The fix, because Bom gave me the look. Say one clear sentence about what you want, every single day. Not a hint. A sentence. Protect your energy: leave a room when it's draining you, politely and without guilt. Write your daydreams down, then go and do one real thing in the world. In love, assume they can't read your mind, because they truly can't. You're the rain: quiet, everywhere, life-giving. You're also allowed to simply say it's raining. Out loud. That's the whole fix. Try it today. Once is enough to start.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gye. 'Maybe' is not an answer. It's a fog machine.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye is just gentle!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gentle, and expecting everyone to be psychic. They're not.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You absorb everyone's mood and then vanish for a week.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye understands people so deeply.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Yes. Now let them understand you. Use a whole sentence.

by_element_balance.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
by_element_balance.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
by_element_balance.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything's urgent, everything's dramatic, and your feelings arrive with sirens on. You're fun and bright, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
by_element_balance.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the colour, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
by_element_balance.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
by_element_balance.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
by_element_balance.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
by_element_balance.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
by_element_balance.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyse it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
by_element_balance.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.
